verdict.rationale: New Relic documents some background automation of its own. The Security RX Agent triages CVEs, drafts remediation plans, and can open Jira or GitHub issues that trigger a coding agent. Alert conditions are user-defined and continuously evaluate signals and route notifications without a user present. There is also a marketing claim of 'automated remediation'. However, nothing documents a general-purpose way for users to build their own autonomous automations or workflows: no custom triggers, schedules, or multi-step actions. Missing for 10: a documented user-configurable automation/workflow builder, details on scheduling or trigger configuration, evidence that the 'automated remediation' claim is substantiated, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: the agent triages the CVE, provides an analysis, drafts step-by-step remediation recommendations
can open a Jira ticket or GitHub issue in the affected repository — triggering a coding agent you already use (such as GitHub Copilot, Claude, or a custom agent) to initiate a fix
You define the data to watch, the thresholds that if exceeded mean an issue, who is notified, and how.
Move beyond assistance to automated remediation.
